title: Least squares to the pseudo-inverse
summary: From the normal equations you derived, through dependent columns and the smallest best fit, to the pseudo-inverse via the singular value decomposition (SVD) and the hard half of Eckart–Young.
written: Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5) on 15 Nov 2026 from docs/seed-context.md. Every answer key is re-derived with sympy by tools/validate_courses.py.

lessons.title: Normal equations from your three points
lessons.summary: A recap built from your own example. Skim it if it feels familiar.

lessons.title: Dependent columns: many best fits
lessons.summary: When one column is a multiple of another, a whole line of fits is equally good.

lessons.title: The smallest best fit
lessons.summary: The point on c + 2m = 3 with the smallest c² + m², and why it is special.

lessons.title: The pseudo-inverse from the SVD
lessons.summary: Build A⁺ from the SVD and see that A⁺b is the smallest best fit.

lessons.title: Why no rank-k matrix does better
lessons.summary: The hard half of Eckart–Young: a small rank forces a null space that meets span(v₁…v_{k+1}).
